candidates.title: Claude Code 2.1.332: MCP servers can ship skills, a PreSkillShellCommand hook, OTel changes, and automatic model fallback
candidates.author: Anthropic
candidates.what_changed: New version 2.1.332 (Edition 4 covered up to 2.1.330). Skills from MCP servers (beta); a PreSkillShellCommand hook that can refuse a skill's or command's inline shell commands as it loads; OpenTelemetry changes; model fallback instead of an error; default model and alias changes on Bedrock, Vertex (Agent Platform) and Foundry.
candidates.mechanism: Added: MCP servers can provide skills (beta), shown as server:skill in the / menu while other skills keep their names. Added the PreSkillShellCommand hook event, which can refuse a skill's or command's inline shell commands as the skill loads (on 2.1.331 and older, a settings file naming the event opens a dialog at start). Added 'Always deliver' to the prompt for held messages from other sessions. Added an OTel assistant_response event for text sent through SendUserMessage or Cowork's message tool when response logging is on. Added the Cyber Verification Program access tier to the startup header. Changed: --model default and a Default pick now step down to an older model when the default isn't available instead of stopping with an error (in auto mode, only to a model auto mode accepts). The sonnet alias is now Sonnet 5.5 on Agent Platform and Foundry, and Foundry's opus alias is Opus 5.5; on Bedrock, sonnet stays at Sonnet 4.5. Foundry's default model is Sonnet 5.5. A bug fix makes the sonnet alias on Bedrock Mantle mean Sonnet 5, where it had resolved to Haiku 4.5. Sessions on Sonnet 5/5.5 on Bedrock Mantle, Agent Platform and Foundry now start in auto mode when no mode is set (opt out with disableAutoMode: "disable"). The default OTel service.name for desktop Code tab sessions is now claude-code-desktop, which breaks filters keyed on claude-code (keep the old name with OTEL_SERVICE_NAME). OTel tool_input now shows only the length of SendUserMessage text unless OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=1. The self-hosted runner's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN prefix can now be oat02- as well as oat01-, so proxy rules and log scrubbers that match oat01- need updating. computer-use is now a reserved skill name on Macs with computer use on. /permissions refuses a rule that would be skipped at the next start (e.g. rm -rf with no tool name). Plan mode in the desktop app and VS Code asks for approval instead of refusing when no auto-mode safety check can judge a command. Fixes (93 in total) include: Read, @-mentions and compaction hanging on a named pipe such as a .env mounted by a locked secrets manager (now fails after 20s); turns ending in 'Prompt is too long' after repeated auto-compaction failures; compaction summaries that ran past the output limit (after three cut-off replies, the last try asks for a shorter summary); freezes from hooks or MCP servers flooding output (hook text over about 50,000 characters is now shortened); SSE MCP servers hanging after a stream reconnect; CLAUDE.md and rules files being sent a second time after a move into a .claude/worktrees worktree; MCP task IDs up to 1,024 characters (was 128); Code Mode silently skipping tool calls whose input has a list of over 4,096 items; Code Mode subagents failing with 'Agent stalled' when a script ran over 10 minutes; recovery when a proxy's request size limit made every message and /compact fail with a 413.
candidates.relevance: high: MCP-provided skills plus a hook gate for skill shell commands ties directly to Edition 4's 'rules file vs gate' theme. The OTel service.name change and the oat02- token prefix are breaking changes for anyone with dashboards or log scrubbers. The model-alias changes affect cost and behavior on clouds.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: The same URL was used in Editions 2-4 (2.1.327 and 2.1.330), but 2.1.331 and 2.1.332 are materially new.
candidates.summary: See mechanism. The best brief angles: (1) skills can now come from MCP servers, and the new PreSkillShellCommand hook lets you refuse their inline shell commands at load time, a supply-chain gate for third-party skills; (2) operators should check for breaking telemetry and auth-string changes (claude-code-desktop service.name, oat02- token prefix, the OTel SendUserMessage redaction); (3) Default/--model now falls back to an older model rather than failing, so an unavailable model no longer stops a run, but you may silently get an older one.

candidates.title: Claude Code 2.1.331: Code Mode on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry; gen_ai.* OTel token attributes; plugin optionalDependencies
candidates.author: Anthropic
candidates.what_changed: Released Nov 23, after Edition 4's 2.1.330 brief. Code Mode is now available in terminal sessions on Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Adds gen_ai.* semantic-convention attributes to llm_request spans, an API connectivity check in claude doctor, a CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION env var, plugin optionalDependencies, and a managed-marketplace auto-update default change coming on or after Nov 30.
candidates.mechanism: Added gen_ai.usage.*, gen_ai.response.model and gen_ai.operation.name to claude_code.llm_request trace spans; gen_ai.usage.input_tokens includes prompt-cache tokens. claude doctor reports API reachability with the HTTP status or error. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION asks for uncompressed responses behind proxies that cut off compressed ones (not yet advised for self-hosted runners or Remote Control). Plugin manifests can declare optionalDependencies, which install with the plugin and can be disabled or uninstalled separately. A PermissionDenied hook's retry: true now tells Claude to retry the refused call only if the user asked for that call. Announced: on or after Nov 30, 2026, plugin marketplaces in managed extraKnownMarketplaces auto-update by default; opt out per entry with "autoUpdate": false. On Windows, an HKLM registry policy outranks managed-settings.json. Fixes (95) include: MCP tool calls hanging up to 30 minutes on malformed replies; Code Mode losing the middle of long script output (Claude now gets a path to the uncut text, anthropics/claude-code#111373); an interrupted plugin update leaving a partial plugin folder (#102186); a rewind deleting files after a failed restore; auto mode refusing to stop a /loop; Workflow agents leaving background shells and MCP servers running; compaction losing part of its summary when the summary quoted certain XML tags; retrying once when a reply goes silent during thinking.
candidates.relevance: high for platform and ops teams: OTel gen_ai attributes enable per-request cost dashboards, and the managed-marketplace auto-update default is a supply-chain policy change with a deadline (Nov 30).
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Code Mode was covered in Edition 2 (code-mode page); this is its expansion to the cloud providers. Otherwise new.
candidates.summary: See mechanism. A suggested brief: 'Managed plugin marketplaces auto-update from Nov 30; opt out per marketplace with autoUpdate:false' plus 'OTel spans now carry gen_ai.usage token counts, including cache tokens.'

candidates.author: GitHub
candidates.what_changed: Issues get statuses (Backlog, Todo, In progress, In review, Done, Not planned, Duplicate), and repository saved views get a board layout.
candidates.mechanism: Automations: linking a draft PR moves an issue to In progress; marking the draft Ready for review moves it to In review; linking an open PR moves it to In review; assigning a user moves it to Todo; assigning an agent moves it to In progress. candidates.title: Your AI Agents Can Multitask. Can You? (How nine people at Every manage context switching across agents)
candidates.author: Arielle Shipper
candidates.paywall: the first sections are readable; possibly metered or partly paywalled further down (UNVERIFIED)
candidates.what_changed: Practitioner patterns for supervising several agents in parallel without losing focus.
candidates.mechanism: Cites a BCG survey of about 1,500 U.S. workers: people overseeing multiple agents were among the most likely to report 'brain fry', with more errors, more decision fatigue and a stronger intention to quit (secondary citation; BCG source not checked). Patterns from staff: (1) keep a running list of every delegated task, where it runs and what you're waiting on, kept on paper or by an orchestrator agent; (2) cap active projects (Lee Knowlton: two active projects, main plus sub; five was draining); split work into agent-verifiable tasks, run in parallel, and judgment tasks, done in a single thread; plan and 'counterplan' before starting; (3) Kieran Klaassen front-loads every decision, sets up to six projects in an hour, and counts any mid-run request for his input as a failure; (4) Paridhi Agarwal runs 3-5 Claude Code sessions with a short fixed skill pipeline (write, check, stop for review before merge) and says 'if I make a skill too complex, the agent gets worse at following it'; (5) Jack Cheng lets agents act alone when the result is reversible, and signs off on publishing, purchases and ambiguous design choices; his agent produces a one-screen HTML decision brief; (6) Jannik Jung spends 15-30 minutes on re-entry, asking for decisions needed rather than a recap, and is building his own orchestrator that gives a daily brief. The article includes copy-paste prompts.
candidates.evidence_quality: practitioner interviews (n=9 at one company); one secondary survey citation
candidates.independent_confirmation: the BCG survey is cited, not checked
candidates.relevance: high for the 'from the builders' / human-in-the-loop ops angle: reversible vs irreversible approval rules; decision-first summaries
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Edition 4 had 'Throughput isn't the bottleneck; direction is' (hRtmV1mCBSE), which is thematically close. Every's style-method piece was in Edition 4; this is a different article.
candidates.summary: See mechanism. The best single takeaway: let agents act alone on reversible actions, have them return a list of decisions you need to make rather than a recap, and keep the skill pipeline short.
